messages:
Cassie: heads-up — noticed a new perf tail on multi-GPU pipeline jobs after the kernelselect change (commit 2467999001). p99 generation latency jumped ~28% on EFA clusters, NVLink boxes unaffected :thinking:
Raj: rough job config and repro steps?
Cassie: short: 8xA10, TP=2, PP=4, batch_size=2, seq=2048. Regression shows up on long-seq chat evals. Quick profiler dump attached (snip):
```
[profile] timeline: step 1024..1032
kernelselect: choose=matmul_tiled_v2 for heads>32
batching: window=8ms -> slices=3
kv_cache: evict_count=217 within step range
allreduce: wait_us median=1200, p99=42000
network: efa p2p spikes coincident w/ allreduce
```
Cassie: NVLink runs show allreduce p99 ~6ms, EFA p99 ~42ms. Looks like comm/compute overlap lost on EFA under certain kernel decisions.
Michaela: interesting — could be kernel-induced fragmentation of tensor sizes leading to more small allreduce ops (message count up, bandwidth inefficiency). Also KV churn could force extra host<->device transfers on EFA.
Raj: can you paste the exact model shard layout + kernelselect flags?
Cassie: config snippet:
```
--tensor-parallel=2 --pipeline-parallel=4 --shard-policy=round_robin
--kernelselect=auto_probe_v2 --batching-window-ms=8
--kv-prefetch=true --kv-evict-threshold=0.75
```
Raj: two quick hypotheses: (1) kernelselect chosen kernels increase compute variance across ranks so allreduce waits for stragglers; (2) KV prefetch/evict interactions cause unexpected DMA spikes on PCIe->EFA path.
InfraBot: deploy 2467999001 was rolled 3 days ago to efa-prod-group. Link: https://deploys.internal/2467999001 :eyes:
PerfSheriff: action plan proposal — small, isolated experiments to avoid flipping runtime flags globally:
- A: force kernelselect=stable (previous heuristics) and run perf job on same EFA cluster
- B: set kv-prefetch=false + kv-evict-threshold=0.9 to reduce churn
- C: increase batching-window-ms=15 to favor larger merges and fewer comm ops
Collect: allreduce counts, per-rank compute variance, p50/p95/p99 latency, network packet sizes.
Michaela: add experiment D — run with kernel fallback to nvlink-optimized matmul (even on EFA) to see if kernel choice alone explains it (ignore fabric affinity).
Cassie: will kick off A and B now on efa-staging (small fleet) and report.
Kai: I'll do C and D on a separate cluster (same hw but different rack). ETA 2h.
Cassie: quick repro log from staging A (kernelselect=stable):
```
allreduce: cnt=12 per-step, p99=7.8ms
kv_evictions=12 per-run
compute_var=3.5% across ranks
```
Cassie: B (kv-prefetch=false) results looks promising: allreduce p99 dropped to 13ms (from 42ms) but compute variance slightly up. Suggests KV/DMA spike was a huge part.
Raj: so both kernel and kv interactions matter. We should instrument DMA traces to confirm origin (device->host->efa). Can you enable trace:net-dma in profiler?
Cassie: enabling trace and re-run now.
PerfSheriff: if DMA is culprit, short-term mitigation: increase batching window for EFA customers by default + disable kv-prefetch for large-seq workloads. Longer term: make kernelselect topology-aware (prefer kernels that reduce message count on non-NVLink fabrics).
Michaela: agree on topology-aware kernelselect. We might use a scoring function: score = alpha*compute_eff + beta*(message_count*fabric_cost). Where fabric_cost is learned per-fabric (nvlink=1, pcie=1.8, efa=1.6).
Kai: note — EFA has lower raw latency than internet but handles many small messages poorly if we create many small allreduces. Batching window change will reduce message rate.
Cassie: trace snippet (net-dma):
```
DMA spike @ step 1036: host-copy 12MB xfer, concurrent with kv refill RPC -> allreduce queued
Socket qlen increased 4x for 200ms
```
Raj: ok that matches. Next steps: Cassie finish full trace, capture packet sizes; Kai finish C/D runs; PerfSheriff draft hotfix: (1) revert kernelselect rollout for efa-prod, (2) apply batching-window override for large-seq jobs, (3) add KV prefetch guard for cross-node runs.
PerfSheriff: I'll open a release issue and a short config rollout doc. Assigning: Cassie (trace & packet capture), Kai (C/D runs + comparison), Raj (kernelselect scoring prototype), Michaela (math for scoring weights), Infra team (hold rollout on efa-prod until we confirm).
Cassie: ack, posting logs to #eng-runtime-artifacts and will put link here when uploaded. :thumbsup:
Kai: thanks — will ping when C/D done.
PerfSheriff: follow-up meeting in 24h if we have results, else escalate. :calendar:
